defect_summary: governance/router.py had 19 route handlers that call the local _identity(authorization) closure and discard the return value, so they could not capability-gate their response content. BFF-REVIEW-QUEUE-REDACTION-REPAIR-001 fixed the review-queue endpoints and its own evidence file flagged GET /bff/management/governance-ledger as a newly discovered, out-of-scope gap (governance_ledger() aggregates evidence_refs from approval_queue/approval_decisions/interventions/audit_events without ever redacting). This task audits all 19 discarded-identity handlers, redacts the 13 whose response actually carries evidence_refs (including the ledger), and documents why the remaining 6 carry no capability-gated content.

baseline_reconstruction.purpose: Acceptance criterion 1 requires publishing, before any change, a table of whether each of the 19 discarded-identity handlers carries unredacted evidence_refs for a low-capability identity. This table was not captured as raw request/response transcripts before implementation began; it is reconstructed here, transparently and after the fact, by re-running the exact same low-capability request against the frozen base commit's router.py and against the fixed HEAD router.py, using the same fixture read-store the regression suite uses. This is a reconstruction, not a retroactively-backdated claim that the table was published pre-implementation.
baseline_reconstruction.method: git show c7a562d0aa87a3b515cc36b10c5fc6e5bd20ad40:services/control-plane/bff/governance/router.py > /tmp/base_governance_router.py; temporarily copy it over the working-tree router.py (verified clean via `git status --short` before and after so no task edits were lost); build create_governance_router() with the same read_surface/capabilities_for_identity wiring as test_governance_evidence_redaction_sweep.py's _SweepStore and auth.policy, issue a GET with Authorization: Bearer op-sweep-1:operator (operator role: holds risk.alert.read only) against each of the 19 routes, and record whether the JSON response contains a ref dict with ref_id in {ref-metric-ev, ref-job-ev} that lacks a `redacted` key (i.e. a capability-gated ref disclosed with no gating annotation at all). Repeat the identical requests against the restored, unmodified HEAD router.py for comparison. get_consult_request and bff_review_validators/get_consult_policy naturally 404 or return policy-only shapes against the minimal fixture store; the check still holds because it inspects the full response body for any disclosed capability-gated ref, not just a specific field path.
baseline_reconstruction.conclusion: All 13 handlers with verdict REDACT above show base_unredacted_capability_gated_ref_present=true and head_unredacted_capability_gated_ref_present=false, confirming both the pre-fix defect and the fix. All 6 handlers with verdict NO_OP_DOCUMENTED show false in both columns, confirming they never disclosed capability-gated evidence and that leaving them unchanged did not introduce a regression.
baseline_reconstruction.worktree_hygiene: `git status --short services/control-plane/bff/governance/router.py` was confirmed empty both immediately before the temporary base-router swap and immediately after restoring the HEAD file, so no task edit was lost or masked by the reconstruction; the reconstruction script itself was a scratch file outside the declared artifact contract and was deleted, not committed.

implementation_note_governance_ledger: GovernanceService.governance_ledger() (service.py) does not accept an identity/capabilities argument. Rather than threading identity through the service layer (which would touch governance/service.py and diverge from every other already-correct handler's pattern of redacting the assembled response in the router), the router now redacts response["data"]["items"] post-hoc with the same _redact_evidence_field_items() helper used elsewhere, after the service call and after the service's own pagination. This keeps the diff scoped to governance/router.py + the new test file and inventory registration -- service.py, human_inbox.py, models.py, auth/policy.py, core/app_factory.py, and management_read_models/service.py are all unchanged, matching the precedent set by BFF-REVIEW-QUEUE-REDACTION-REPAIR-001. Flagging for reviewer preference: pushing this into the service layer (for symmetry with consult_memo_projection/mutation_review_projection, which redact inside service.py) is a viable alternative if a future task wants ledger-source-level redaction instead of response-shape redaction.
governance_ledger_dedup_note: governance_ledger() keys entries by f"ledger-approval-{decision_id}" via dict.setdefault, so when the same decision_id appears in both approval_queue_items and approval_decisions, only the first-seen (queue-sourced) entry survives in the ledger; the decisions-sourced entry for that id is dropped. This is pre-existing service.py behavior, not introduced or changed by this task. Regression coverage in test_governance_evidence_redaction_sweep.py is written against this actual dedup behavior (one approval-queue-sourced entry, one intervention entry, two audit entries) rather than four independently-observable per-id ledger rows.
fix_summary: services/control-plane/bff/governance/router.py: added two shared redaction helpers inside create_governance_router() alongside the existing _safe_redact/_redact_review_queue_items from BFF-REVIEW-QUEUE-REDACTION-REPAIR-001: _redact_evidence_field_items(identity, items, field="evidence_refs") for flat lists of dicts carrying a top-level evidence-ref list (approval decisions/queue, audit events, ledger entries, transcript events), and _redact_consultation_metadata_evidence(identity, items) for session-shaped dicts carrying metadata.consultation.evidence_refs (consultation session/participants/outcome). Fixed the 13 handlers above: each now assigns identity = _identity(authorization) (previously discarded) and routes its evidence-bearing payload through one of the two helpers -- always after any pagination/page-slicing has already happened, so redacted_evidence_count covers only the returned page. Every withheld ref carries redacted:true, required_capability, reason="insufficient_capability" (BFF-FINAL-007 shape, produced by the pre-existing, unchanged models.redact_evidence_refs/RedactedEvidenceRef). Fails closed: _safe_redact (unchanged) substitutes an empty capability set on any capability-lookup failure, so every capability-gated ref is withheld rather than disclosed. The 6 no-op handlers were left discarding identity, each with a documented reason above for why their response carries no capability-gated content. No changes to models.py, auth/policy.py, core/app_factory.py, governance/service.py, governance/human_inbox.py, or management_read_models/service.py -- the canonical redaction policy owner and its wiring were already correct; only router.py needed the missing calls.

regression_coverage_added.harness: Builds the real create_governance_router() directly (never imports main), wired exactly like core/app_factory.py: redact_evidence_refs=models.redact_evidence_refs, capabilities_for_identity=auth.policy.capabilities_for_identity, extract_identity=auth.policy.extract_identity. No class-level monkeypatching of domain services -- a minimal read-store double (_SweepStore) supplies fixture rows with mixed alert/metric/job evidence_refs.
coverage: Every one of the 13 fixed handlers exercised with a low-capability identity (operator role: holds risk.alert.read, lacks metric.read and job.read) asserting the metric/job refs are withheld (redacted:true, required_capability, reason=insufficient_capability) while the alert ref passes through, and the correct redacted_evidence_count is reported.

Every fixed handler is also exercised with a full-capability identity (admin role), each asserting both the exact unredacted evidence_refs payload (equal to the original mixed-refs fixture, not merely inferred from a zero count) and redacted_evidence_count == 0 -- including get_approval_decision_detail, get_consultation, and get_consultation_participants, which previously only had fail-closed coverage for the full-capability path, not an actual successful passthrough assertion.
list_governance_approval_queue paginated across two pages (page_size=1) asserting redacted_evidence_count reflects only the item on the returned page, not the full unpaginated set.

Fail-closed coverage for get_approval_decision_detail, bff_management_governance_ledger, and get_consultation_participants: capabilities_for_identity raising -> every capability-gated ref withheld even for an identity that would otherwise have full capabilities.

bff_management_governance_ledger coverage across all four evidence sources feeding the ledger (approval_queue_items, approval_decisions -- subject to the dedup behavior noted above, v5_interventions, governance_audit_events), plus a dedicated decision-only-entry test (test_governance_ledger_includes_decision_only_approval_entry) that supplies an approval id present only in the approval_decisions dataset (never in approval_queue_items) and asserts its ledger entry reports source_dataset=approval_decisions with correct low-capability redaction and full-capability passthrough -- distinct from the existing dedup test, which is unchanged and still covers the same-id-in-both-datasets shadowing behavior.
